title: Images' "Reacting to environment changes" doesn't reflect reality
body: According to https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reacting-to-environment-changes UAs should end up firing a load event if either the current source or the selected density changes. Consider the following test-case: ```html ``` According to the spec you should not fire a load event, since the source and selected density are the same as the last selected source and last selected density. Yet Blink and WebKit at least do fire it (bug? maybe, but let's keep going). No UA triggers loads when the selected density changes as a result of the sizes attribute, which doesn't follow the spec, but I think it's the right thing to do. Testcase: ```html ``` So the current state of things is: * Nothing changes, nobody triggers extra loads (yay, matches the spec). * Source URL changes, everybody triggers the load (yay, matches the spec). * Only density changed: No extra load event (doesn't match the spec, but matches all implementations). * `` changed, but the URL and density are the same: Blink / WebKit fire an extra load event, FF doesn't (I think FF is right here). * `` changed, but the URL is the same, and density changes: Everyone triggers a new load. I'm changing Firefox as part of https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1149357 to at least being consistent with itself and don't trigger it. Note I haven't tested Edge. So, there's a clear lack of interop here. I propose not queuing a new image load unless the URL has changed, making density only relevant for presentation. That's Gecko's behavior after https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1149357, so I might be biased, but I also think it's what looks saner to prevent UAs potentially tons of loads during viewport resize, and what I think I'd expect as an author. cc @annevk
